key_insight: Somatic mutations can be summarized as continuous, gene-level disruption across protein and regulatory functions, revealing cancer biology beyond classic driver hotspots.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help identify patients with biologically meaningful tumor-gene disruption and associated survival differences, even when canonical hotspot mutations are absent.
method: Applied AlphaGenome and AlphaMissense to somatic variants from 8,800 TCGA patients across 33 cancer types.
Aggregated variant-level scores into patient-gene disruption profiles for transcription, chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, and splicing.
Compared disruption patterns by cancer type, tissue of origin, microsatellite instability, and survival outcomes.
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 8,800 patients and 33 cancer types in TCGA, with an independent treatment-annotated cohort used to evaluate survival associations.
watch_item: These are model-derived predictions rather than direct functional measurements, so clinical use would require external validation and careful context-specific interpretation.
paper_title: Genomic foundation model-derived disruption profiling links somatic mutations to cancer biology and clinical outcomes
